magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is in accordance with the Catholic emphasis on fatherly presence and responsibility toward the family: Mislav consciously rearranges his work to be more present with his wife and daughter, without asserting that everyone must make the same decision. Prudent planning of income and time can serve the family's good, provided that the real needs of the family are responsibly cared for.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Pope Francis points out that a father should be close to his wife and children and that presence is not the same as control; the emphasis on time for the family therefore has a strong pastoral foundation. Catholic teaching does not require a specific reduction of income from everyone, but a deliberate use of work and material goods in the service of family duties and love of neighbors.

sections.subtitle_en: Birth of a Daughter and a 70 Percent Cut in Income
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mislav explains the decision to reduce income by 70% for the sake of the family
sections.content_en:
His wife's words coincided with the **birth of his daughter**, when Mislav made a big decision. What he otherwise does for business clients, which are structures, risk assessments, and business plans, he applied to his own life. He put everything into spreadsheets, strategy, and steps, and **cut 70 percent of all income**. As he says, that is **70 percent of time that he must get for his wife and daughter**, because he wants to be the best dad and the best husband, and the old way of life "leads nowhere anymore."

He explains that with money he never wanted to prove anything to anyone or show off in a Ferrari. He measured his worth by how much he can save and earn so that the family would be safe. When he realized that meant nothing to them, because **"obviously we weren't well, and there was money,"** he saw that he was reliving the problems of his first, primary family and repeating its patterns. His primary family today is the one he forms with his wife and child, and they do not have to live that scenario.

He calculated how much is necessary for them to live and to invest in the estate they are renovating and made a life and business pivot. Something surprising turned out: **all along he was able to work 70 percent less and have the same income.** "We returned to the old path, only we decided to work smarter," says Mislav.

sections.subtitle: Ne služiti Bogu i bogatstvu: vrijednost izvan dobivenih i izgubljenih projekata
sections.screenshot_description: Mislav govori o vjeri kao mjerilu vrijednosti umjesto zarade
sections.content:
Mislav naglašava da mu ni ta promjena nije davala vrijednost. Vodi ga vjera, i to poznata misao da **čovjek ne može služiti Bogu i bogatstvu**. „Moje bogatstvo u mom srcu je Bog i vjera, sve ovo ostalo služi meni“, kaže. Pravilo mu je jednostavno: **ako on počne služiti onome što radi, umjesto da to služi njemu, takvo se što „reže instant“ iz života.**

To nastoji osvještavati svakodnevno, **kroz molitvu i pokušaj da se duhovno i objektivno sagleda izvana**. Upozorava da je lako vratiti se starim obrascima jer suvremeno doba, preko društvenih mreža, televizije i vijesti, uči ljude da štuju ono što bi im trebalo služiti.

Priznaje i što mu se zapravo događalo prije povratka vjeri. **Svaki dobiveni projekt govorio mu je „vrijedan si“, a svaki izgubljeni „nisi vrijedan, moraš ponovno zaslužiti poštovanje prema sebi“.** To je, kaže, bio „krivi pattern cijelo vrijeme“, a riješio ga je, hvala Bogu, njegov povratak vjeri.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak uglavnom vjerno izražava Isusovo upozorenje da se Bogu i bogatstvu ne može služiti kao dvama gospodarima te ispravno prepoznaje opasnost da posao i novac postanu mjerilo osobne vrijednosti. Ipak, izraz da „sve ostalo služi meni” može zvučati previše usmjereno na vlastitu korist: kršćanski je naglasak da materijalna dobra nisu gospodari, ali da se njima upravlja odgovorno i za dobro obitelji i bližnjih.
concerns: Izraz „sve ovo ostalo služi meni” mogao bi se protumačiti kao da je osobna korist jedino mjerilo uporabe dobara; katoličko shvaćanje upraviteljstva uključuje i ljubav prema bližnjemu.
Pravilo da se ono čemu osoba počne služiti „reže instant” može biti korisno kao osobna odluka, ali ne treba ga pretvoriti u opće pravilo koje zanemaruje razborito razlučivanje i postojeće obveze.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusove riječi o Bogu i bogatstvu ne znače da je svako posjedovanje novca ili imovine samo po sebi grijeh: upozorenje je usmjereno na njihovo idoliziranje i na zatvaranje srca Bogu i potrebitima. Papa Ivan Pavao II. zato povezuje slobodu od tiranije bogatstva s ljubavlju prema Bogu i bližnjemu; molitva i preispitivanje vlastitih motiva mogu pomoći da posao ostane sredstvo odgovornog služenja, a ne izvor vlastite vrijednosti.

“What is Man?” (Ps 8:5). An itinerary of biblical anthropology
1 March 1987: Pastoral visit to the parish of "SS. Nome di Maria" of Rome - Homily

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage mostly faithfully expresses Jesus' warning that one cannot serve God and wealth as two masters, and correctly identifies the danger of work and money becoming the measure of personal worth. However, the phrase that "everything else serves me" may sound overly focused on self-interest: the Christian emphasis is that material goods are not masters, but that they are to be managed responsibly and for the good of the family and neighbors.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' words about God and wealth do not mean that any possession of money or property is in itself a sin: the warning is directed against their idolization and against closing the heart to God and the needy. Pope John Paul II therefore connects freedom from the tyranny of wealth with love of God and neighbor; prayer and examination of one's own motives can help keep work a means of responsible service rather than a source of self-worth.
concerns_en: The phrase "all this other stuff serves me" could be interpreted as if personal benefit were the sole criterion for using goods; the Catholic understanding of stewardship also includes love of neighbor.

The rule that what a person begins to serve is "cut instantly" can be useful as a personal decision, but it should not be turned into a general rule that disregards prudent discernment and existing obligations.

sections.subtitle_en: Not Serving God and Wealth: Worth Outside of Won and Lost Projects
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mislav speaks about faith as a measure of worth instead of earnings
sections.content_en:
Mislav emphasizes that even that change did not give him worth. He is guided by faith, and that the well-known thought that **man cannot serve God and wealth**. "My wealth in my heart is God and faith, all the rest of this serves me," he says. His rule is simple: **if he begins serving what he does, instead of it serving him, such a thing is "cut instantly" from life.**

He strives to become aware of this daily, **through prayer and an attempt to view himself spiritually and objectively from the outside**. He warns that it is easy to return to old patterns because the modern era, through social media, television, and news, teaches people to worship what should serve them.

He also admits what was actually happening to him before returning to the faith. **Every won project told him "you are worthy," and every lost one "you are not worthy, you have to earn respect for yourself again."** That, he says, was "the wrong pattern the entire time," and it was resolved, thank God, by his return to the faith.

sections.subtitle: Socijalistički odgoj i bunt protiv riječi „moraš“
sections.screenshot_description: Mislav opisuje socijalistički odgoj i vlastiti bunt protiv tog obrasca
sections.content:
Marko pita dolazi li taj obrazac vrednovanja sebe kroz uspjeh iz obitelji. Mislav odgovara da ne nužno, iako se to uvijek naglašavalo. Njegova je obitelj živjela vjeru, dok je on tada nije živio na isti način. Bez obzira na to, odgajani su, kako on to voli reći, **„socijalistički“**: zaposli se, cijeli život budi u jednoj firmi i u kancelariji, primaj plaću i bit će ti dobro, budi dobar radnik i slušaj što ti se govori.

Protiv toga se Mislav pobunio. „Neće meni nitko govoriti što ja moram“, govorio je, jer za njega **„moraš“ ne postoji**. Ironija je u tome što je taj pritisak onda počeo nametati sam sebi i, kako zaključuje, **„sam sebi postao najveći neprijatelj“**.

Ozbiljnu temu Fran prekida šalom vraćajući se na Petrokemiju. Nudi Mislavu da mu „sredi“ umjetno gnojivo za imanje i dodaje: „Evo, postat ću uspješan.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak prikazuje osobno iskustvo pritiska i pobune, a ne izričito naučava da su obveze same po sebi loše; prepoznavanje da je govornik taj pritisak počeo nametati sam sebi može otvoriti prostor za zdravije razlučivanje. Ipak, ako bi se tvrdnja da „moraš“ ne postoji uzela kao opće načelo, bila bi u napetosti s kršćanskim shvaćanjem moralnih obveza i odgovorne poslušnosti.
concerns: Izjava „moraš ne postoji“ može zvučati kao odbacivanje svake obveze; katoličko shvaćanje slobode ne izjednačuje slobodu s neograničenim samoodređenjem, nego je povezuje s istinom, dobrom i odgovornim izborom.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanska poslušnost nije slijepo prihvaćanje svakog ljudskog zahtjeva: autoritet treba služiti i razumno usmjeravati, a poslušnost ne ukida slobodu nego je može staviti u službu dobra. Apostolski poziv djeci na poslušnost roditeljima također je ograničen izrazom „u Gospodinu“, dok roditelji ne smiju svoju vlast provoditi tako da djecu obeshrabre ili pretjerano opterete.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage depicts a personal experience of pressure and rebellion rather than explicitly teaching that obligations are bad in themselves; recognizing that the speaker began imposing that pressure on himself can open space for healthier discernment. Still, if the claim that "'must' does not exist" were taken as a general principle, it would be in tension with the Christian understanding of moral duties and responsible obedience.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Christian obedience is not blind acceptance of every human demand: authority must serve and guide reasonably, and obedience does not eliminate freedom but can place it at the service of the good. The apostolic call to children to obey their parents is also qualified by the phrase "in the Lord," while parents must not exercise their authority in a way that discourages or overly burdens their children.
concerns_en: The statement "'must' does not exist" can sound like a rejection of every obligation; the Catholic understanding of freedom does not equate freedom with unlimited self-determination, but connects it with truth, the good, and responsible choice.

sections.subtitle_en: Socialist Upbringing and Rebellion Against the Word "Must"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mislav describes a socialist upbringing and his own rebellion against that pattern
sections.content_en:
Marko asks whether that pattern of evaluating oneself through success comes from the family. Mislav answers not necessarily, although it was always emphasized. His family lived the faith, while he at that time did not live it in the same way. Regardless of that, they were brought up, as he likes to put it, **"socialistically"**: get a job, be in one company and in an office your whole life, receive a salary and you will be fine, be a good worker and listen to what you are told.

Against that Mislav rebelled. "Nobody is going to tell me what I must do," he would say, because for him **"must" does not exist**. The irony is in the fact that he then began imposing that pressure on himself and, as he concludes, **"became the greatest enemy to himself."**

Fran interrupts the serious topic with a joke returning to Petrokemija. He offers to Mislav to "arrange" artificial fertilizer for his estate and adds: "Here, I will become successful."

sections.subtitle: Kućni budžet bez iluzija: „Znam koliko mi treba za život“
sections.screenshot_description: Fran objašnjava kako on i supruga vode kućni budžet
sections.content:
Nakon što je Mislav opisao kako je godinama vlastitu vrijednost mjerio novcem, voditelj Marko isto pitanje postavlja Franu: kako on povezuje svoje prihode i osjećaj uspjeha?

Fran priznaje da je došao do stanja uma u kojem točno zna **koliko mu treba za život** i koliko on i supruga ulažu u zajednički kućni budžet. Kaže da pokušavaju štedjeti što je više moguće, ali da im to trenutno slabo ide, pa ga supruga zna „napasti“ zbog trošenja. Otvoreno govori i o razdoblju u kojem se obitelj nalazi. S dolaskom djeteta troškovi rastu, pa su posegnuli za ušteđevinom koju šaljivo naziva „crnim fondom“. Drugi posao ne želi tražiti dok mu to ne postane prijeko potrebno.

Iz te svakodnevne, prizemne slike Fran prelazi na ono što ga u odnosu prema novcu najviše oblikovalo: iskustvo davanja desetine.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak opisuje obiteljsko planiranje prihoda, štednje i troškova bez tvrdnje da novac određuje osobnu vrijednost, pa je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naglaskom na odgovornom upravljanju dobrima i brizi za obitelj. Budući da se iskustvo davanja desetine tek najavljuje, taj dio njegova odnosa prema novcu nije moguće teološki ocijeniti na temelju ovog odlomka.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk smatra opravdanim da obitelj raspolaže prihodima razborito i stvara ušteđevinu koja joj može pomoći u potrebi; štednja je dobra kada služi sigurnosti i dostojnom životu, a ne pohlepi ili gomilanju kao svrsi samoj sebi. Mjerilo nije samo visina prihoda, nego i pravedno uzdržavanje obitelji, solidarnost i izbjegavanje rasipnosti.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage describes family planning of income, savings, and expenses without asserting that money determines personal worth, so it is mostly aligned with the Catholic emphasis on responsible management of goods and care for the family. Since the experience of tithing is only being introduced, that part of his attitude toward money cannot be theologically evaluated based on this passage.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching considers it justified for a family to manage income prudently and build savings that can assist in time of need; saving is good when it serves security and a dignified life, not greed or hoarding as an end in itself. The measure is not merely the level of income, but just provision for the family, solidarity, and avoiding wastefulness.

sections.subtitle_en: Household Budget Without Illusions: "I Know How Much I Need for Life"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran explains how he and his wife manage the household budget
sections.content_en:
After Mislav described how for years he measured his self-worth with money, the host Marko poses the same question to Fran: how does he connect his income and the sense of success?

Fran admits that he reached a state of mind in which he knows exactly **how much he needs for life** and how much he and his wife invest in the joint household budget. He says that they try to save as much as possible, but that it is currently going poorly for them, so his wife knows how to "attack" him because of spending. He also speaks openly about the period in which the family finds itself. With the arrival of a child expenses grow, so they reached for the savings that he jokingly calls the "black fund." He does not want to look for a second job until it becomes an absolute necessity for him.

From that everyday, down-to-earth image Fran moves to what shaped him most in his relationship toward money: the experience of giving the tithe.

sections.subtitle: Desetina iz praznog džepa: „Kušajte i vidite kako je dobar Gospodin“
sections.screenshot_description: Fran prepričava kako je dao desetinu dok je radio kao konobar
sections.content:
Fran se vraća u vrijeme kad je bio gotovo bez posla. Radio je kao konobar tek tri dana u mjesecu. Kad bi platio studentski dom, ostajalo bi mu, kako sam kaže, jedva stotinjak eura u džepu. Ne snalazi se najbolje s točnim iznosima i šali se da mu matematika nikad nije bila jača strana. Marko je u to vrijeme na susretima zajednice stalno poticao na davanje desetine, a Fran se pitao: „Što da ti dam?“

Odricanje od tog dijela novca bilo mu je iznimno teško. Želio je sudjelovati u zajednici u kojoj se obratio i u kojoj služi, ali je strahovao kako će preživjeti mjesec. Na kraju se odlučio na iskorak vođen riječima **„kušajte i vidite kako je dobar Gospodin“**. Odlučio je „iskušati“ Boga i dati desetinu.

Ubrzo mu je prišao prijatelj iz zajednice s kojim se tek bio upoznao i rekao da je dobio poticaj da mu da novac. Bilo je to oko 300 kuna, u vrijeme prelaska s kuna na eure. Fran se isprva nećkao, kao kad „dođe neka tetka iz Njemačke“ pa joj govoriš da ne treba. Prijatelj je inzistirao. Potom mu je nešto prebacio i Marko, pa i mama, iako, ističe Fran, nikoga ništa nije tražio. Do kraja mjeseca na računu mu se našlo **trostruko ili četverostruko** više nego što je dao. Isti mu je prijatelj pomogao i oko posla, pa se idući mjesec zaposlio u njegovoj firmi.

Od tada je desetina za Frana obavezna. Ranije bi davao samo ako mu nešto ostane na kraju mjeseca, „dva eura“. Danas, čim mu sjedne plaća, 10% ide zajednici.

magisterium.assessment: Svjedočanstvo uglavnom izražava kršćansko povjerenje u Božju dobrotu i velikodušno sudjelovanje u životu zajednice; Psalmistov poziv „kušajte i vidite“ poziva na pouzdanje u Gospodina, a ne na puko teorijsko znanje o njemu. Ipak, opis davanja kao „iskušavanja“ Boga i naglašavanje da se novac višestruko vratio mogu se shvatiti kao obećanje materijalne nagrade, što bi zamaglilo razliku između povjerenja u providnost i trgovine s Bogom.
concerns: „Kušajte i vidite“ biblijski je poziv da se iskusi Božja dobrota i utočište u njemu, a ne uputa da se Boga iskušava financijskim postupkom ili očekivanjem određenog ishoda.

Povrat novca i zaposlenje jesu dio osobnog svjedočanstva, ali ne treba ih prikazivati kao zajamčenu posljedicu davanja desetine: Isusov poziv na povjerenje u providnost nije obećanje da će vjernik uvijek dobiti materijalnu nadoknadu.

Riječ „obavezna“ može zvučati kao da je deset posto obvezujuće pravilo za svakog katolika; dostavljeni biblijski i crkveni tekstovi podupiru povjerenje i traženje Božjega kraljevstva, ali ne utvrđuju takvu univerzalnu stopu.
magisterium.enrichment: Psalm 34 poziva vjernika da se osloni na Gospodina, a Katekizam opisuje Kristov poziv kao sinovsko povjerenje u Očevu providnost. To povjerenje nije pasivnost niti jamstvo da će se svaka potreba riješiti očekivanim novčanim priljevom: kršćanin surađuje s providnošću i velikodušno dijeli, ali svoju nadu ne veže uz izračunatu financijsku korist.

magisterium.assessment_en: The testimony mostly expresses Christian trust in God's goodness and generous participation in community life; the Psalmist's invitation "taste and see" calls for reliance on the Lord, not mere theoretical knowledge of Him. However, describing giving as "testing" God and emphasizing that the money was returned manifold can be understood as a promise of material reward, which would blur the line between trust in providence and bargaining with God.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Psalm 34 calls the believer to rely on the Lord, and the Catechism describes Christ's call as filial trust in the Father's providence. This trust is neither passivity nor a guarantee that every need will be resolved by an expected influx of money: the Christian cooperates with providence and shares generously, but does not tie their hope to calculated financial benefit.
concerns_en: "Taste and see" is a biblical call to experience God's goodness and refuge in Him, not an instruction to test God through a financial action or expectation of a specific outcome.

The return of money and finding employment are part of personal testimony, but they should not be presented as a guaranteed consequence of tithing: Jesus' call to trust in providence is not a promise that the believer will always receive material reimbursement.

The word "mandatory" can sound as if ten percent is a binding rule for every Catholic; the provided biblical and ecclesial texts support trust and seeking the Kingdom of God, but do not establish such a universal rate.

sections.subtitle_en: Tithe Out of an Empty Pocket: "Taste and See How Good the Lord Is"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran recounts how he gave a tithe while working as a waiter
sections.content_en:
Fran returns to the time when he was almost without a job. He worked as a waiter only three days a month. When he would pay for the student dormitory, there remained for him, as he says himself, barely a hundred euros or so in his pocket. He doesn't do best with exact amounts and jokes that math was never his strong suit. Marko at that time constantly encouraged giving the tithe at community meetings, and Fran wondered: "What should I give you?"

Giving up that part of the money was extremely difficult for him. He wanted to participate in the community in which he converted and in which he serves, but he feared how he would survive the month. In the end he decided on a step forward guided by the words **"taste and see how good the Lord is."** He decided to "test" God and give the tithe.

Soon a friend from the community with whom he had just gotten acquainted approached him and said that he received an impulse to give him money. It was around 300 kunas, at the time of transition from kunas to euros. Fran at first hesitated, as when "some aunt from Germany comes" and you tell her that she doesn't need to. The friend insisted. Then Marko also transferred something to him, and even mom, although, Fran emphasizes, he asked nobody for anything. By the end of the month there was **threefold or fourfold** more in his account than what he gave. The same friend also helped him regarding a job, so the next month he got employed in his company.

From then on the tithe is obligatory for Fran. Earlier he would give only if something was left over for him at the end of the month, "two euros." Today, as soon as his salary hits, 10% goes to the community.

sections.subtitle: „Tražite najprije kraljevstvo Božje“: životna teza o novcu
sections.screenshot_description: Fran citira Evanđelje po Mateju o pticama nebeskim i ljiljanima
sections.content:
Kad je riječ o novcu, Fran se uvijek vraća na šesto poglavlje Evanđelja po Mateju. Navodi da su to otprilike retci od 24. do 30., uz ogradu da nije siguran u točne brojeve. Riječ je o odlomku o pticama nebeskim i ljiljanima u polju, koji vrhunac ima u poruci **„Tražite najprije kraljevstvo Božje, a sve ostalo će vam se nadodati.“**

To mu je, kaže, životna teza. Ako mu je Bog na prvom mjestu i ako mu predaje cijeli svoj život, siguran je da će sve biti dobro. Priznaje da je znalo biti trenutaka u kojima se pitao hoće li im biti dovoljno, no ne pamti mjesec u kojem su doista strepili za preživljavanje. Redovito bi „drugi dan sjela uplata“, a u tome prepoznaje „Božji prst“.

Tu je poruku prenio i mlađem bratu. Za krizmu mu nije dao čestitku, nego mu je kupio džepnu Bibliju, a novčanicu od 100 eura stavio upravo na stranicu s tim citatom. „Pitaj Boga je li ikad otvorio“, šali se Fran.

Naglašava ipak da desetina nije trgovina s Bogom:

- ne daje se zato što će Bog „vratiti sve te novce“,
- nego zato što je **Bog vrijedan** toga da mu se da dio prihoda,
- i zato što se Riječ treba čuti, a zajednica razvijati.

Čovjek se mjesec dana čudi Božjoj providnosti, pa zaboravi, pa opet da, pa mu se opet vrati. „Samo trebaju ljudi biti dovoljno hrabri da sve puste“, zaključuje.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s Isusovim naukom: Matej 6 poziva da se najprije traže Božje kraljevstvo i njegova pravednost te da se ne živi u tjeskobi zbog materijalnih potreba. Dobro je što Fran izričito odbacuje shvaćanje desetine kao trgovine s Bogom, no tvrdnja da će „sve biti dobro“ može zvučati kao jamstvo nesmetanog materijalnog blagostanja, što Isusov tekst ne obećava.
concerns: Matej 6,33 ne treba tumačiti kao obećanje da vjernik neće iskusiti oskudicu ili neizvjesnost; odlomak poziva na povjerenje u Oca i prvenstvo njegova kraljevstva, a ne na sigurnost da će se sve odvijati prema željenom materijalnom ishodu.

Isusov poziv da se ne brinemo pretjerano ne znači zanemariti odgovorno planiranje i rad; katoličko tumačenje razlikuje tjeskobnu zaokupljenost od razborite brige, a providnost poziva na suradnju, ne na pasivno čekanje.
magisterium.enrichment: U Mateju 6 Isus neposredno prije poziva na traženje kraljevstva upozorava da se ne može služiti i Bogu i bogatstvu, pa je središnja tema prvenstvo Boga, a ne obećanje financijskog uspjeha. Povjerenje u Oca oslobađa od pretjerane tjeskobe, ali ne isključuje odgovorno djelovanje; crkveno tumačenje providnosti naglašava da vjernici surađuju s Božjim djelom.

Catechism of the Catholic Church

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mostly aligned with Jesus' teaching: Matthew 6 calls one to seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and not to live in anxiety over material needs. It is good that Fran explicitly rejects viewing tithing as bargaining with God; however, the assertion that "everything will be fine" can sound like a guarantee of unhindered material prosperity, which Jesus' text does not promise.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Matthew 6, immediately prior to calling for seeking the kingdom, Jesus warns that one cannot serve both God and wealth, so the central theme is the primacy of God, not a promise of financial success. Trust in the Father frees from excessive anxiety, but does not exclude responsible action; ecclesial interpretation of providence emphasizes that believers cooperate with God's work.
concerns_en: Matthew 6:33 should not be interpreted as a promise that the believer will not experience hardship or uncertainty; the passage calls for trust in the Father and the primacy of His kingdom, not for certainty that everything will unfold according to a desired material outcome.

Jesus' call not to worry excessively does not mean neglecting responsible planning and work; Catholic interpretation distinguishes anxious preoccupation from prudent concern, and providence calls for cooperation, not passive waiting.

sections.subtitle_en: "Seek First the Kingdom of God": A Life Thesis on Money
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran quotes the Gospel of Matthew about the birds of the air and the lilies
sections.content_en:
When it comes to money, Fran always returns to the sixth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew. He states that those are roughly verses 24 to 30, with a caveat that he is not sure about the exact numbers. It is about the passage on the birds of the air and the lilies in the field, which has its climax in the message **"Seek first the Kingdom of God, and all these things will be added to you."**

That, he says, is his life thesis. If God is in the first place for him and if he surrenders his whole life to him, he is sure that everything will be well. He admits that there were moments in which he wondered whether it would be enough for them, but he does not remember a month in which they truly trembled for survival. Regularly "the next day a payment would arrive," and in that he recognizes the "finger of God."

He passed that message on to his younger brother as well. For confirmation he did not give him a greeting card, but bought him a pocket Bible, and put a 100-euro banknote precisely on the page with that quote. "Ask God whether he ever opened it," Fran jokes.

He emphasizes nevertheless that the tithe is not a bargain with God:

- it is not given because God will "return all that money,"
- but because **God is worthy** of having a part of the income given to him,
- and because the Word needs to be heard, and the community needs to develop.

A person marvels at God's providence for a month, then forgets, then gives again, then it is returned to him again. "People just need to be brave enough to let go of everything," he concludes.

sections.subtitle: Zaruke bez sređenog života: prvo iskorak, pa sredstva
sections.screenshot_description: Fran priča o trenutku kad je kleknuo pred Paulu
sections.content:
Fran priznaje da pomalo „ide predaleko u temu“, ali želi dodati još jedno iskustvo. Kad je kleknuo pred Paulu i zaprosio je, nije imao sređen život niti „10.000 na računu“, a ni sliku o tome što će biti idućih deset godina.

Za prsten nije ciljano štedio. Mama je prodala staru kuću i dio novca podijelila djeci. Kad su mu ta sredstva sjela na račun, odlučio je od njih kupiti prsten, a za ostalo će „vidjeti“. Nakon toga se, kaže, sve počelo slagati: **najprije je donio odluku, a onda su stizala sredstva** potrebna da je ostvari.

Iz toga izvlači pouku koju želi prenijeti slušateljima. Život ne mora biti savršen ni posložen da bi se donosile velike odluke. Bog, smatra, čovjeka često baci „u vatru“ i pita ga hoće li se odlučiti.

Isti savjet davao je i kamermanu podcasta kad je ovaj trebao zaprositi djevojku. Ne mora najprije srediti posao ni dovesti „deset klijenata“. Ako osjeća da je trenutak pravi i da su oboje spremni za brak, treba napraviti prvi korak, a „ove stvari sa strane“ doći će poslije.

magisterium.assessment: Poruka da zaruke ne treba odgađati dok život ne postane savršen može biti u skladu s kršćanskim povjerenjem i hrabrošću za trajnu odluku, osobito jer se savjet uvjetuje time da su oboje spremni za brak. Ipak, formulacija „prvo odluka, pa sredstva“ može zvučati kao da je financijska i životna odgovornost sporedna ili da će Bog nužno providjeti konkretna sredstva nakon odluke.
concerns: Zaruke su put priprave i sazrijevanja, a ne zamjena za razlučivanje: ne bi ih trebalo požurivati samo zato što okolnosti nikada nisu idealne. Papa Franjo upozorava da se koraci prema braku ne smiju žuriti i da je razdoblje zaruka vrijeme upoznavanja, zajedničkog planiranja i priprave.
Osobno iskustvo u kojem su sredstva došla nakon odluke ne može se pretvoriti u opće obećanje da će Bog nakon svake velike odluke osigurati novac ili ukloniti praktične teškoće.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razlučivanje ne traži savršene okolnosti, ali traži slobodnu, promišljenu odluku i ozbiljnu pripravu za doživotni bračni savez. Stoga je korisno razlikovati „ne čekati idealne uvjete“ od „zanemariti odgovorno planiranje“: posao ili određena svota na računu nisu sami po sebi uvjet za zaruke, ali razgovor o zajedničkom životu, odgovornostima i realnim mogućnostima pripada zreloj pripravi.

citations.document_title: General Audience of 27 May 2015: The family - 16. Engagement
Acta Apostolicae Sedis: Issue 10, October, 2013

magisterium.assessment_en: The message that engagement should not be postponed until life becomes perfect can be aligned with Christian trust and the courage for a permanent decision, especially since the advice is conditioned on both being ready for marriage. Still, the phrasing "first the decision, then the means" can sound as though financial and life responsibility are secondary or that God will necessarily provide concrete means following the decision.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic discernment does not seek perfect circumstances, but requires a free, deliberate decision and serious preparation for a lifelong marital covenant. Therefore, it is helpful to distinguish "not waiting for ideal conditions" from "disregarding responsible planning": a job or a specific sum in an account are not in themselves conditions for engagement, but discussing shared life, responsibilities, and realistic possibilities belongs to mature preparation.
concerns_en: Engagement is a path of preparation and maturation, not a substitute for discernment: it should not be rushed simply because circumstances are never ideal. Pope Francis warns that steps toward marriage must not be rushed and that the engagement period is a time of getting to know one another, mutual planning, and preparation.
A personal experience in which means arrived after the decision cannot be turned into a general promise that God will provide money or remove practical difficulties following every major decision.

sections.subtitle_en: Engagement Without an Orderly Life: First the Step Forward, Then the Means
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran talks about the moment he knelt before Paula
sections.content_en:
Fran admits that he is slightly "going too far into the topic," but wants to add one more experience. When he knelt before Paula and proposed to her, he did not have an orderly life nor "10,000 in the account," nor a picture of what would be in the next ten years.

He did not purposely save for the ring. Mom sold an old house and distributed part of the money to the children. When those funds landed in his account, he decided to buy the ring with them, and for the rest he would "see." After that, he says, everything began falling into place: **first he made a decision, and then the means necessary to realize it were arriving**.

From that he draws a lesson that he wants to convey to the listeners. Life does not have to be perfect nor sorted out for big decisions to be made. God, he believes, often throws a person "into the fire" and asks him whether he will make a decision.

He gave the same advice to the podcast cameraman when he was supposed to propose to his girlfriend. He doesn't have to sort out the job first nor bring "ten clients." If he feels that the moment is right and that both are ready for marriage, he should take the first step, and "these things on the side" will come afterward.

sections.subtitle: „Tko gleda na oblake, ne sije“: okolnosti nikad nisu idealne
sections.screenshot_description: Marko citira Knjigu Propovjednikovu o oblacima i sijanju
sections.content:
Marko na Franovo iskustvo nadovezuje citat iz Knjige Propovjednikove: **„Tko gleda na oblake, ne sije nikad.“** Tko uvijek promatra okolnosti, nikad ništa neće napraviti, jer one nikad nisu idealne. Uvijek nešto čeka i uvijek „bi trebalo“ još nešto.

Priča i o prijatelju čije je riječi slušao kad je imao dvadesetak godina. Na što god bi se taj prijatelj oslonio kao na sigurnost, Bog bi mu to „izbio“. Zato se, govorio je, boji i pomisliti na ušteđevinu koju ima na računu, da je ne bi izgubio. Ta slika lažnog oslonca Marku je ostala urezana.

Zatim iznosi osobno iskustvo od prije dvije godine. Financijska situacija im se taman malo popravila, a supruga Mirjana došla je s poticajem da trebaju dati određeni iznos. Prva mu je reakcija bila „disaj, prodisat ću“. Mirjana ga je tada pitala: da mu je predložila da te novce stave u otplatu kredita, bi li pristao? „Nema šanse, ne bih ni trećinu“, odgovorio je. Pa zašto je onda na ovo pristao? „Više vjerujem Bogu nego stanju na računu“, rekao je.

Naglašava da ni to nije bila trgovina. Očekivao je da će upisi u jedan od tadašnjih programa nakon tog iskoraka „roknuti“, a dogodilo se suprotno: „nikad gore, nijedan upis“. Tada je zastao i rekao: „Bože, šta god bilo, ti si dostojan ovog iskoraka, čak i ako se ništa od ovoga ne dogodi.“

magisterium.assessment: Tumačenje Propovjednika kao upozorenja protiv beskonačnog čekanja na idealne okolnosti dobro odgovara biblijskom retku i može poticati hrabrost, povjerenje i velikodušnost. Osobito je teološki zdravo što Marko izričito odbacuje trgovinu s Bogom i prihvaća darivanje čak i ako ne uslijedi očekivani uspjeh.
concerns: Anegdota da Bog prijatelju redovito „izbija“ ono na što se oslanja može, ako se shvati kao opće pravilo, pogrešno prikazati Boga kao onoga koji kažnjava svaku financijsku sigurnost ili namjerno uzrokuje gubitke kako bi čovjeku oduzeo oslonac. To je osobno tumačenje događaja, a ne zaključak koji proizlazi iz navedenog biblijskog retka.

Povjerenje u Boga ne znači da svako darivanje treba učiniti bez razboritog razmatranja vlastitih obveza i potreba obitelji; opisani primjer ne daje dovoljno podataka za procjenu je li iznos bio primjeren.
magisterium.enrichment: Propovjednik 11,4 doista upozorava da onaj tko stalno promatra vjetar neće sijati, a tko gleda oblake neće žeti; redak ohrabruje djelovanje usred neizvjesnosti, ali ne jamči određeni financijski ishod. Kršćanska velikodušnost zato može biti čin povjerenja i zahvalnosti, a ne ulaganje kojim se od Boga očekuje povrat: Markov zaključak da je Bog dostojan dara i ako se upisi ne povećaju jasno izražava upravo tu razliku.

citations.document_title: The Holy Bible
citations.document_author: The New Revised Standard Version, Catholic Edition (NRSV-CE)

magisterium.assessment_en: Interpreting Ecclesiastes as a warning against endlessly waiting for ideal circumstances corresponds well to the biblical verse and can encourage courage, trust, and generosity. It is especially theologically sound that Marko explicitly rejects bargaining with God and accepts giving even if the expected success does not follow.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Ecclesiastes 11:4 indeed warns that whoever constantly observes the wind will not sow, and whoever looks at the clouds will not reap; the verse encourages action in the midst of uncertainty, but does not guarantee a specific financial outcome. Christian generosity can therefore be an act of trust and gratitude rather than an investment by which a return is expected from God: Marko's conclusion that God is worthy of the gift even if enrollments do not increase clearly expresses precisely this distinction.
concerns_en: The anecdote that God regularly "knocks out" what a friend relies on can, if taken as a general rule, mistakenly portray God as one who punishes every financial security or deliberately causes losses to strip a person of support. That is a personal interpretation of events, not a conclusion arising from the cited biblical verse.

Trust in God does not mean that every act of giving should be done without prudent consideration of one's own obligations and family needs; the described example does not provide enough data to judge whether the amount was appropriate.

sections.subtitle_en: "Whoever Watches the Clouds Does Not Sow": Circumstances Are Never Ideal
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko quotes the Book of Ecclesiastes about clouds and sowing
sections.content_en:
Marko connects a quote from the Book of Ecclesiastes to Fran's experience: **"Whoever watches the clouds never sows."** Whoever always observes circumstances will never do anything, because they are never ideal. One is always waiting for something and always "there should be" something more.

He also speaks about a friend whose words he listened to when he was around twenty years old. Whatever that friend leaned on as security, God would "knock out" for him. That is why, he would say, he fears even thinking about the savings he has in his account, lest he lose them. That image of a false crutch remained etched in Marko's memory.

Then he presents a personal experience from two years ago. Their financial situation had just improved a bit, and his wife Mirjana came with an impulse that they should give a certain amount. His first reaction was "breathe, I'll catch my breath." Mirjana then asked him: if she had proposed that they put that money into paying off the loan, would he have agreed? "No chance, not even a third," he answered. So why then did he agree to this? "I trust God more than the state of the account," he said.

He emphasizes that this was not a trade either. He expected that enrollments into one of the then-programs after that step forward would "skyrocket," but the opposite happened: "never worse, not a single enrollment." Then he stopped and said: "God, whatever happens, you are worthy of this step forward, even if none of this happens."

sections.subtitle: Financije otkrivaju u što vjerujemo
sections.screenshot_description: Marko govori o pritisku društvenih mreža na mlade muškarce
sections.content:
Marko prenosi misao jednog propovjednika: **financije pokazuju u što čovjek vjeruje**. One otkrivaju ima li povjerenja i u koga ga ima, u iznos na računu, ušteđevinu i vlastitu sigurnost ili u Boga.

Upravo tu vidi posebno muško opterećenje. Svijet i društvene mreže nameću status: moraš zaraditi, moraš imati određeni sat, određeni auto, a ako ne uspiješ, nešto s tobom nije u redu. Mladim se dečkima reklamira „sloboda“ u kojoj se ne radi ništa, a novca ima napretek. Onda se čovjek „ubije od posla“ i pita je li budala, treba li skrenuti u nekretnine ili neki drugi model zarade.

Božja je perspektiva, ističe Marko, potpuno drugačija i uvijek polazi od pitanja **kakav život čovjek želi živjeti**. Mnogi obrasci o kojima su govorili dolaze iz obitelji, iz onoga što je netko gledao kao dijete i u kakvom je okruženju odrastao.

Osvrće se i na Mislavljevo iskustvo. Mislav se pobunio protiv nametnutog modela „zaposli se i slušaj“, ali je ipak upao u obrazac, samo u drugom obliku. „Ne možeš ti od obrasca pobjeći“, zaključuje Marko. Obrazac ostaje u čovjeku dok ga ne definira i ne počne se svjesno izvlačiti iz njega.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak da novac može razotkriti gdje čovjek traži sigurnost dobro se slaže s biblijskim pozivom da se uzda u Boga, a ne da materijalna dobra postanu njegovo konačno uporište. Ipak, financijske odluke same po sebi nisu potpuna mjera vjere, a povjerenje u Providnost ne znači zanemariti rad, odgovorno planiranje ili razboritu brigu za obitelj.
concerns: Tvrdnja da financije pokazuju u što čovjek vjeruje može biti korisna duhovna provjera, ali postaje preširoka ako se iz nje zaključuje o nečijoj vjeri samo na temelju prihoda, štednje ili načina trošenja.
Formulacija da se od obrasca ne može pobjeći mogla bi zvučati deterministički; odlomak je ublažava time što govori o prepoznavanju obrasca i svjesnom radu na izlasku iz njega.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusov poziv na pouzdanje u Oca ne nalaže pasivnost: kršćanin ne treba živjeti u tjeskobnom robovanju novcu, ali je pozvan surađivati s Providnošću i najprije tražiti Božje kraljevstvo. Zato novac može biti povod za ispit savjesti—služi li dobru osobe i obitelji ili postaje izvor identiteta i gospodarenja životom—ali ne i samostalan dokaz nečije svetosti.

citations.document_title: 1 March 1987: Pastoral visit to the parish of "SS. Nome di Maria" of Rome - Homily
General Audience of 24 March 1999
Acta Apostolicae Sedis: Issue 11, November, 1995

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis that money can reveal where a person seeks security aligns well with the biblical call to trust in God rather than making material goods one's ultimate anchor. Still, financial decisions in themselves are not a complete measure of faith, and trust in Providence does not mean neglecting work, responsible planning, or prudent care for the family.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' call to trust in the Father does not mandate passivity: the Christian should not live in anxious slavery to money, but is called to cooperate with Providence and seek first the Kingdom of God. Therefore, money can be an occasion for an examination of conscience—whether it serves the good of the person and family or becomes a source of identity and mastery over life—but not an independent proof of someone's holiness.
concerns_en: The assertion that finances show what a person believes in can be a helpful spiritual check, but it becomes overly broad if one infers someone's faith solely from income, savings, or spending patterns.
The formulation that one cannot escape the pattern could sound deterministic; the passage tempers this by speaking of recognizing the pattern and consciously working to exit it.

sections.subtitle_en: Finances Reveal What We Believe In
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko talks about the pressure of social media on young men
sections.content_en:
Marko conveys the thought of a preacher: **finances show what a person believes in**. They reveal whether one has trust and in whom one has it, in the amount in the account, savings, and one's own security, or in God.

It is precisely there that he sees a particular male burden. The world and social media impose status: you have to earn, you have to have a certain watch, a certain car, and if you don't succeed, something is wrong with you. Young guys are advertised "freedom" in which nothing is worked, and money is plentiful. Then a man "kills himself from work" and wonders if he is a fool, whether he should turn to real estate or some other model of earning.

God's perspective, Marko emphasizes, is completely different and always starts from the question **what kind of life a person wants to live**. Many patterns about which they spoke come from the family, from what someone watched as a child and in what environment one grew up.

He also reflects on Mislav's experience. Mislav rebelled against the imposed model "get a job and listen," but still fell into a pattern, only in a different form. "You cannot run away from a pattern," Marko concludes. A pattern remains in a person until one defines it and begins consciously pulling oneself out of it.

sections.subtitle: Kad supruga zarađuje više: tetovaže, jednobojna majica i klijenti po svom
sections.screenshot_description: Mislav prepričava odluku da se tetovira usprkos upozorenjima
sections.content:
Marko otvara osjetljivo pitanje: što ako muškarac zarađuje manje od svoje žene? Mislav odgovara bez zadrške. Nema nikakav problem s tim, a sve je, kaže, u komunikaciji, kao i u odnosu s Bogom. Fran se odmah našali da bi ostao doma s djetetom kad bi Paula zarađivala 10.000 eura, a Marko dobacuje da sjede s „new age muškarcima“.

Mislav svoj stav ilustrira jednom zanimljivošću iz vlastite karijere. Prije mnogo godina, kad je ulazio u industriju, odlučio se tetovirati. Tetovaže su tada još bile svojevrsni tabu i svi su ga upozoravali da neće naći posao. Odgovorio je: **„Tko me ne želi istetoviranog, ja s tim ne želim raditi.“** Upravo mu je to otvorilo vrata u zabavnoj i glazbenoj industriji.

Kad je kasnije počeo raditi s korporacijama, odbio je odijela. Klijentima je poručivao da će s njim raditi u jednobojnoj majici i trapericama jer znaju da im on može pomoći, a ne zbog sata ili odijela. „Uvijek sam izgledao kao klošar, i uvijek je bilo para, i uvijek su mi dolazili pravi ljudi, jer sam birao s kim ću raditi“, kaže. Priznaje i da je bilo pogrešnih odabira klijenata, često upravo zbog novca.

Poanta je jasna. Ako je takva postava u obitelji i ako se supružnici dogovore da jedno ide „all in“ ili da dijele 50-50, sve je u redu, dok god su oni dobro.

Marko dodaje da mnogi muškarci s tim imaju problem jer to doživljavaju kao udarac na osjećaj vrijednosti, a Fran procjenjuje da je takvih danas velika većina. Marko pak kaže da se iskreno raduje Mirjaninim uspjesima.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak ispravno ne poistovjećuje muževljevu vrijednost s time da zarađuje više od supruge te ističe komunikaciju i zajednički dogovor, što je sukladno dostojanstvu i uzajamnoj odgovornosti supružnika. Moguća je nejasnoća u tvrdnji da je sve prihvatljivo dok god su oni dobro: bračni dogovor treba vrednovati i prema uzajamnom darivanju, obvezama prema djeci i dobru obitelji, a ne samo prema subjektivnom zadovoljstvu.
concerns: Izraz „dok god su oni dobro” može se protumačiti preusko ako zanemari dobro djece, pravednu podjelu odgovornosti, međusobno poštovanje ili obveze koje proizlaze iz braka.

Tetovaže, odjeća i biranje klijenata predstavljeni su kao osobne profesionalne odluke, a ne kao mjerilo moralnosti; važno je ne zaključiti da neformalni izgled ili određeni stil rada sam po sebi donosi Božju naklonost ili financijski uspjeh.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički pogled na brak ne veže dostojanstvo supružnika uz tržišni uspjeh niti uz unaprijed zadanu podjelu zarade, nego uz vjernost, uzajamno poštovanje i nesebično darivanje. Crkveni nauk naglašava da supružnici zajednički razlučuju odluke i uzimaju u obzir potrebe, duhovni rast i obiteljske obveze; stoga se model prihoda može razlikovati od para do para, ali treba služiti njihovu zajedničkom dobru.

citations.document_title: General Audience of 29 April 2015: The family - 12. Marriage (I)
The Bible and Morality: Biblical Roots of Christian Conduct
Mulieris Dignitatem

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage rightly does not equate a husband's worth with earning more than his wife, and highlights communication and mutual agreement, which is consistent with the dignity and mutual responsibility of spouses. There is potential ambiguity in the assertion that everything is acceptable as long as they are well: marital agreements must also be evaluated according to mutual self-giving, obligations to children, and the good of the family, not solely by subjective satisfaction.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic view of marriage does not tie the dignity of spouses to market success or to a predetermined division of earnings, but to fidelity, mutual respect, and selfless giving. Church teaching emphasizes that spouses discern decisions together and take into account needs, spiritual growth, and family obligations; thus the model of income can vary from couple to couple, but must serve their common good.
concerns_en: The expression "as long as they are well" can be interpreted too narrowly if it disregards the good of children, fair division of responsibilities, mutual respect, or obligations arising from marriage.

Tattoos, clothing, and choosing clients are presented as personal professional choices, not as a standard of morality; it is important not to conclude that an informal appearance or a certain work style in itself brings God's favor or financial success.

sections.subtitle_en: When the Wife Earns More: Tattoos, a Plain T-Shirt, and Clients on One's Own Terms
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mislav recounts the decision to get tattooed despite warnings
sections.content_en:
Marko opens a sensitive question: what if a man earns less than his wife? Mislav answers without hesitation. He has no problem whatsoever with that, and everything is, he says, in communication, as in the relationship with God. Fran immediately jokes that he would stay home with the child if Paula earned 10,000 euros, and Marko chimes in that they are sitting with "new age men."

Mislav illustrates his stance with an interesting detail from his own career. Many years ago, when he was entering the industry, he decided to get tattooed. Tattoos were then still a kind of taboo and everyone warned him that he would not find a job. He answered: **"Whoever does not want me tattooed, I do not want to work with them."** It was precisely that which opened doors for him in the entertainment and music industry.

When he later began working with corporations, he rejected suits. He told clients that they would work with him in a plain T-shirt and jeans because they know that he can help them, and not because of a watch or a suit. "I always looked like a bum, and there was always money, and the right people always came to me, because I chose with whom I would work," he says. He also admits that there were wrong choices of clients, often precisely because of money.

The point is clear. If that is the arrangement in the family and if the spouses agree that one goes "all in" or that they share 50-50, everything is fine, as long as they are okay.

Marko adds that many men have a problem with that because they perceive it as a blow to their sense of worth, and Fran estimates that today such men are the great majority. Marko, on the other hand, says that he genuinely rejoices in Mirjana's successes.

sections.subtitle: Čežnja za natjecanjem i propuštena prilika za fast food
sections.screenshot_description: Marko priča o prilici da prije osam godina kupi fast food
sections.content:
Na šaljivo pitanje bi li on ostao kod kuće, Marko odgovara da je previše uključen u projekte. Voli rad s ljudima i ne bi se mogao izolirati, koliko god ponekad za tim „vapi“.

Priznaje i nešto neočekivano. Nikad nije ušao u korporativni svijet, ali je ponekad **čeznuo za tim iskustvom natjecanja i nadmetanja**. U katoličkom okruženju, kaže, ne može nekome reći „želim biti bolji od tebe“. To nije ponizno, a i svi rade na istoj stvari, pa tu nadmetanja nema. Fran se odmah našalio da će poslije snimanja organizirati utrku na 100 metara.

Marko objašnjava da je od 19. ili 20. godine potpuno posvećen istom putu. Krenuo je na jedan fakultet, promijenio ga i završio teologiju. Nema drugo radno iskustvo, pa je prolazio faze prihvaćanja da je to njegov jedini put, a znatiželja kako bi bilo drugdje ostajala je.\n
Prije otprilike osam godina bio je blizu kupnje jednog fast fooda. Vlasnik je prodavao cijeli posao, cijena je bila prihvatljiva, a lokacija idealna: kod Cvjetnog i Studentskog doma, preko puta prostora u kojem je tada „još Vjesnik bio živ“. Prije odluke nazvao je još jednu osobu za mišljenje. Ta mu je rekla da je ponuda dobra, ali da onda neće moći raditi ono što sada radi. Marko je shvatio da ne želi odustati od svog poziva i pustio je priliku.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim razumijevanjem poziva: Marko promišlja o mogućem poslovnom putu i odustaje od njega jer smatra da bi ga udaljio od sadašnjeg poziva, a ne zato što je poslovno poduzetništvo samo po sebi manje vrijedno. Ipak, njegova tvrdnja da u katoličkom okruženju nema prostora za nadmetanje može zvučati kao da je svako natjecanje nespojivo s poniznošću, što nije nužno slučaj.
concerns: Moguće je preširoko poistovjećivanje natjecanja sa sebičnom željom da se bude bolji od drugih; zdravo nastojanje za izvrsnošću može služiti drugima i općem dobru.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni nauk priznaje poduzetništvo kao mogući ljudski i kršćanski poziv te ga vrednuje prema tome služi li ljudskom dostojanstvu i općem dobru, a ne samo financijskom uspjehu. Upozorenje na „iscrpljujuću borbu za nadmoć“ odnosi se na natjecanje koje čovjeka zarobljava egoizmom, a ne na svako nastojanje da se vlastiti darovi razvijaju i koriste na dobro drugih.

citations.document_title: To the entrepreneurs of Ferrara (September 22, 1990) - Speech

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mostly aligned with the Catholic understanding of vocation: Marko reflects on a possible business path and abandons it because he considers that it would distance him from his current calling, not because business entrepreneurship is inherently less valuable. Still, his assertion that in a Catholic environment there is no room for competition can sound as though any competition is incompatible with humility, which is not necessarily the case.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Church teaching recognizes entrepreneurship as a possible human and Christian vocation and evaluates it according to whether it serves human dignity and the common good, not merely financial success. The warning against an "exhausting struggle for dominance" refers to competition that ensnares man in egoism, not to every effort to develop one's gifts and use them for the good of others.
concerns_en: An overly broad equation of competition with a selfish desire to be better than others is possible; a healthy pursuit of excellence can serve others and the common good.

sections.subtitle_en: Longing for Competition and a Missed Opportunity for Fast Food
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko talks about the opportunity to buy a fast food business eight years ago
sections.content_en:
To the humorous question whether he would stay at home, Marko answers that he is too involved in projects. He loves working with people and would not be able to isolate himself, no matter how much he sometimes "cries out" for that.

He also admits something unexpected. He never entered the corporate world, but he sometimes **longed for that experience of competition and rivalry**. In a Catholic environment, he says, you cannot say to someone "I want to be better than you." That is not humble, and also everyone is working on the same thing, so there is no rivalry there. Fran immediately joked that after the recording he would organize a 100-meter race.

Marko explains that since age 19 or 20 he has been completely dedicated to the same path. He started at one faculty, changed it, and graduated in theology. He has no other work experience, so he went through phases of accepting that this was his only path, while curiosity about how it would be elsewhere remained.

About eight years ago he was close to buying a fast food business. The owner was selling the entire business, the price was acceptable, and the location ideal: near Cvjetno and the Student Dormitory, across from the premises where at that time "Vjesnik was still alive." Before making the decision, he called one more person for an opinion. That person told him that the offer was good, but that then he wouldn't be able to do what he does now. Marko realized that he did not want to give up on his calling and let the opportunity go.

sections.subtitle: Ni „sveti par“ ne funkcionira sam od sebe
sections.screenshot_description: Marko govori o tome da na braku treba raditi i u neprofitnom sektoru
sections.content:
Marko upozorava da posao izvan korporativnog svijeta ne jamči zdrave odnose. „Nije da se u ovom svemu ne izgubim“, priznaje. I on i Mirjana znaju se izgubiti, tražiti i „loviti“. Rad u neprofitnom sektoru, ovisnost o donacijama i sve što uz to ide nose posebnu vrstu opterećenja.

Iako izvana možda izgleda posloženo i odmaknuto od svjetovnog mentaliteta uspjeha, i on mora slagati svoje obrasce i odnos s Mirjanom. Mora paziti i učiti obitelj stavljati na prvo mjesto. Zaključuje: **na obiteljskim odnosima treba raditi bez obzira na poziciju**. Nitko automatski ne postaje „sveti par“ kod kojeg sve funkcionira.

Fran nudi drugačije čitanje. Marko je, smatra, rano shvatio kakav mu život odgovara i zato gura ono što voli. Fran i Mislav dolaze iz iskustva u kojem im nešto nije odgovaralo i u kojem su tražili više vremena kod kuće, pa zato i drugačije razmišljaju. Marko to prihvaća kratkim „možda“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je snažno usklađen s katoličkim naukom jer odbacuje pretpostavku da je rad u neprofitnom ili vjerskom okruženju sam po sebi jamstvo svetosti te naglašava svakodnevnu odgovornost za brak i obitelj. Ustrajno ulaganje u odnose i priznavanje da nitko automatski ne postaje „sveti par“ dobro izražavaju kršćansko shvaćanje braka kao poziva koji se živi i raste kroz vrijeme.
magisterium.enrichment: Biblijsko-moralna refleksija o braku ističe uzajamnu odgovornost supružnika, nesebičnu ljubav, rješavanje nesuglasica i trajno obnavljanje bračne predanosti; zato opisani rad na odnosu nije tek praktični dodatak, nego dio življenja bračnog poziva. Kršćanski obiteljski život uključuje slušanje, strpljivost i male svakodnevne službe, a sakramentalna milost podupire supružnike, ali ne znači da će teškoće nestati bez njihova slobodnog i postojanog sudjelovanja.

citations.document_title: The Bible and Morality: Biblical Roots of Christian Conduct
Kristus eina pro šalį
Acta Apostolicae Sedis: Issue 7, July, 2022

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is strongly aligned with Catholic teaching because it rejects the assumption that working in a non-profit or religious environment is in itself a guarantee of holiness, and emphasizes daily responsibility for marriage and family. Persistent investment in relationships and acknowledging that no one automatically becomes a "holy couple" well express the Christian understanding of marriage as a vocation that is lived and grows over time.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Biblical-moral reflection on marriage highlights the mutual responsibility of spouses, selfless love, resolving disagreements, and ongoing renewal of marital dedication; therefore, the described work on the relationship is not merely a practical addition, but part of living the marital vocation. Christian family life involves listening, patience, and small daily services, and sacramental grace supports the spouses, but does not mean difficulties will disappear without their free and steadfast participation.

sections.subtitle_en: Even a "Holy Couple" Does Not Function on Its Own
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko talks about how marriage needs to be worked on in the non-profit sector as well
sections.content_en:
Marko warns that a job outside the corporate world does not guarantee healthy relationships. "It's not that I don't lose myself in all of this," he admits. Both he and Mirjana know how to get lost, search, and "chase." Work in the non-profit sector, dependence on donations, and everything that goes with it carry a special kind of burden.

Although from the outside it might look arranged and detached from the worldly mentality of success, he too must arrange his patterns and relationship with Mirjana. He must pay attention and learn to put the family in the first place. He concludes: **family relationships need to be worked on regardless of position**. Nobody automatically becomes a "holy couple" where everything functions.

Fran offers a different reading. Marko, he believes, realized early what kind of life suits him and therefore pushes what he loves. Fran and Mislav come from an experience in which something did not suit them and in which they sought more time at home, so they also think differently. Marko accepts that with a short "maybe."

sections.subtitle: Osigurati obitelj ne znači samo financirati je
sections.screenshot_description: Mislav objašnjava razliku između osiguravanja i financiranja obitelji
sections.content:
Mislav polazi od načela: ni muškarac ni žena nemaju što kome dokazivati, ni sebi ni supružniku. „Nitko ti ne stavlja kruh na stol osim tebe“, ponavlja. Zadaća muža i žene, kakav god bio njihov dogovor, jest **osigurati zdrav dom**.

Tu, kaže, muškarci najčešće griješe. Kad čuju „osigurati obitelj“, misle na „financirati obitelj“. Prihod je, međutim, samo jedna stavka, „jedan boks“. Uz njega su tu i:

- odnosi unutar obitelji,
- stabilnost i sigurnost koje se pružaju kroz odnos sa supružnikom,
- odnos s djecom.

O svemu tome ovisi je li netko doista osigurao obitelj ili je samo netko tko je financira. Upravo je od toga Mislav odlučio pobjeći. Shvatio je da je njegovo „radim za obitelj“ zapravo značilo raditi 12 do 15 sati dnevno i „grčiti pare“. Kad dođe kući, u najboljem bi se slučaju posvađao sa ženom, a inače bi samo otišao spavati pa se ne bi ni vidjeli.

To mu je bio najgori scenarij i pitao se želi li takav biti kao otac i muž. Tek nakon zaokreta shvatio je koliko zapravo mogu smanjiti. Želja za više je normalna, ističe, ali treba se zapitati **dokle ide ambicija, koliko je više stvarno potrebno i zašto**.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je snažno usklađen s katoličkim razumijevanjem obiteljske odgovornosti: uz materijalno uzdržavanje ističe uzajamnu ljubav, stabilnost i prisutnost roditelja, a neograničenu ambiciju podvrgava dobru obitelji. To što muž i žena mogu dogovoriti kako će tu odgovornost ostvarivati odgovara naglasku na njihovoj zajedničkoj i uzajamnoj odgovornosti.
concerns: Izraz „Nitko ti ne stavlja kruh na stol osim tebe“ mogao bi, izdvojen iz konteksta, zvučati kao da se uzdržavanje svodi isključivo na samostalnost pojedinca; kršćansko razumijevanje rada uključuje i odgovornost prema obitelji, uzajamnu pomoć i povjerenje u Boga.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk ne suprotstavlja pošten rad obiteljskom životu: rad može osiguravati uzdržavanje i stabilnost obitelji, ali ne bi smio postati jedino mjerilo uspjeha niti narušavati obiteljske odnose. Drugi vatikanski sabor opisuje brak kao zajedrništvo u kojem supružnici kasvaju uzajamnom ljubavlju i posvećenjem, dok crkveni tekstovi upozoravaju da potrošačka težnja za sve većim posjedovanjem može nauditi braku i obitelji.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is strongly aligned with the Catholic understanding of family responsibility: alongside material provision, it emphasizes mutual love, stability, and parental presence, subjecting unrestrained ambition to the good of the family. The fact that husband and wife can agree on how to realize this responsibility corresponds to the emphasis on their shared and mutual responsibility.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching does not oppose honest work to family life: work can provide support and stability for the family, but should not become the sole measure of success nor damage family relationships. The Second Vatican Council describes marriage as a communion in which spouses grow through mutual love and sanctification, while church texts warn that consumerist striving for ever greater possessions can harm marriage and the family.
concerns_en: The phrase "Nobody puts bread on the table except you" could, taken out of context, sound as if provision were reduced exclusively to individual self-reliance; the Christian understanding of work also includes responsibility toward the family, mutual assistance, and trust in God.

sections.subtitle_en: Providing for the Family Does Not Mean Only Financing It
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mislav explains the difference between providing for and financing a family
sections.content_en:
Mislav starts from the principle: neither a man nor a woman has anything to prove to anyone, neither to themselves nor to their spouse. "Nobody puts bread on the table except you," he repeats. The task of husband and wife, whatever their agreement might be, is to **ensure a healthy home**.

There, he says, men most often make a mistake. When they hear "provide for the family," they think of "financing the family." Income is, however, only one item, "one box." Alongside it there are also:

- relationships within the family,
- stability and security provided through the relationship with the spouse,
- the relationship with the children.

On all of this depends whether someone has truly provided for the family or is merely someone who finances it. It was precisely from that that Mislav decided to run away. He realized that his "I work for the family" actually meant working 12 to 15 hours a day and "scrambling for cash." When he would come home, in the best case he would argue with his wife, and otherwise he would just go to sleep so they wouldn't even see each other.

That was the worst scenario for him and he wondered whether he wanted to be like that as a father and husband. Only after the pivot did he realize how much they can actually cut back. The desire for more is normal, he points out, but one should ask oneself **how far ambition goes, how much more is really necessary, and why**.

sections.subtitle: „Biznis i Biblija“: koliko je dosta?
sections.screenshot_description: Marko spominje knjigu Biznis i Biblija
sections.content:
Marko se prisjeća prve knjige koju je pročitao nakon obraćenja, a to je bila „Biznis i Biblija“. Autor u njoj tvrdi da čovjek u nekom trenutku mora **definirati koliko mu je dosta**. On je to učinio za sebe, a sve iznad toga daje.

Isti je pristup, priča Marko, primijenio i jedan njegov prijatelj, uspješan poduzetnik. Nije bio „stisnut“ niti si je zadavao kruta pravila poput „samo jedan auto“ ili „ne više od jednog stana“. Dao si je oduška i odredio što smatra prihvatljivim. Ipak, s obzirom na svoje mogućnosti živi vrlo skromno, a sve iznad postavljene granice spreman je dati, i doista daje.

Marko podsjeća i na mudrost koja se često spominje kad je riječ o financijama: **kod susjeda je trava možda zelenija, ali je i račun za vodu veći**. Želja za više donosi i više umora.

Pitanje zatim okreće prema gostima. Fran je odrastao uz oca koji je bio stalno prisutan kod kuće, a sam neće moći ispuniti tu sliku. Fran se šali da mu je cilj do 30. „otići u mirovinu s 28“. Marko odgovara da bi njemu to bilo kao da su mu „odsjekli noge“ i postavlja ključno pitanje: **tko si ti, Mislave, ako ne možeš ostvariti ono o čemu sanjaš?**

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom jer razboritu mjeru u stjecanju dobara povezuje sa skromnošću i spremnošću na darivanje, umjesto s gomilanjem bogatstva. Pitanje o identitetu i neostvarenim snovima otvara važnu temu, ali ne izriče jasno da se čovjekova vrijednost ne mjeri poslovnim uspjehom ni postignućima.
concerns: Unaprijed određena granica onoga što je „dosta“ može biti razborit osobni kriterij, ali ne bi trebala postati kruto pravilo koje zanemaruje promjenjive obiteljske obveze, pravednu naknadu za rad ili druge odgovornosti.
Formulacija o tome tko je čovjek ako ne ostvari san može se shvatiti kao poziv na razmišljanje, ali bez dodatnog pojašnjenja riskira povezati identitet i osobnu vrijednost s postignućem.
magisterium.enrichment: Biblijska mudrost upozorava da život ne ovisi o obilju posjeda i poziva na dijeljenje dobara, dok istodobno ne tvrdi da je svako bogatstvo samo po sebi zlo; problem nastaje kad novac postane predmet pohlepe ili idol. Katolički pogled na rad i poduzetništvo zato drži dobit nužnom, ali je ne smatra krajnjom svrhom, nego je prosuđuje prema dobru osobe, obitelji i zajednice. Čovjekovo dostojanstvo ne proizlazi samo iz onoga što postiže: kršćanski poziv uključuje i primanje života i milosti kao dara.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mostly aligned with Catholic teaching because it connects prudent moderation in acquiring goods with modesty and readiness to give, rather than accumulating wealth. The question regarding identity and unfulfilled dreams opens an important topic, but does not explicitly state that a person's worth is not measured by business success or achievements.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Biblical wisdom warns that life does not depend on an abundance of possessions and calls for sharing goods, while at the same time not claiming that all wealth is evil in itself; the problem arises when money becomes the object of greed or an idol. The Catholic view of work and entrepreneurship therefore considers profit necessary, but does not see it as the ultimate end, judging it instead according to the good of the person, family, and community. Human dignity does not stem solely from what one achieves: the Christian calling also includes receiving life and grace as a gift.
concerns_en: A predetermined limit of what is "enough" can be a prudent personal criterion, but should not become a rigid rule disregarding changing family obligations, just compensation for work, or other responsibilities.

The formulation regarding who a person is if they do not achieve a dream can be understood as an invitation to reflect, but without further clarification risks linking identity and personal worth to achievement.

sections.subtitle_en: "Business and the Bible": How Much Is Enough?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko mentions the book Business and the Bible
sections.content_en:
Marko recalls the first book he read after his conversion, which was "Business and the Bible." The author in it claims that a person at some point must **define how much is enough for him**. He did that for himself, and everything above that he gives away.

The same approach, Marko recounts, was also applied by a friend of his, a successful entrepreneur. He wasn't "stingy" nor did he set rigid rules for himself like "only one car" or "no more than one apartment." He gave himself leeway and determined what he considers acceptable. Still, considering his means, he lives very modestly, and everything above the set limit he is ready to give, and indeed gives.

Marko also recalls the wisdom often mentioned when it comes to finances: **the neighbor's grass might be greener, but the water bill is also higher**. The desire for more brings more fatigue as well.

He then turns the question toward the guests. Fran grew up with a father who was constantly present at home, and he himself will not be able to fulfill that image. Fran jokes that his goal by 30 is to "retire at 28." Marko replies that for him that would be as if they had "cut off his legs" and poses the key question: **who are you, Mislav, if you cannot achieve what you dream of?**

sections.subtitle: Tko sam bez titule? Sin Božji, suprug i tata
sections.screenshot_description: Mislav govori da se na konferencijama prvo predstavlja kao sin Božji, suprug i tata
sections.content:
Mislav kaže da je to pitanje morao postaviti sam sebi i da je čest motiv u njegovim videima. Odgovor je potražio na papiru. Na jednu stranu stavio je sve čega bi se mogao odreći: mogućnost kupnje imanja, njegovu obnovu, financije, posao. Na drugu stranu napisao je ono što doista želi. Ponavljalo se jedno: **više vremena s obitelji, zdrav odgoj djeteta i zdrav odnos sa ženom**.

Shvatio je da je sve čega se odriče vezano uz nešto novčano i ovozemaljsko, što mu kao osobi ne daje nikakvu vrijednost. „Još je gore“, priznaje, jer se nije dokazivao drugima nego sebi.

Danas, kad govori na konferencijama i predavanjima, ne navodi najprije titulu. Kaže: **„Ja sam prije svega sin Božji, želim biti suprug, želim biti tata.“** To što je konzultant samo je način na koji osigurava egzistenciju. Mogao je biti bilo što, a odabrao je ono što zna raditi. Bilo bi „malo bez veze“ sada učiti za tesara, „iako bi bilo cool“.

Postavio je i jasnu granicu, kako kaže, „cap“. Ako mu posao ponovno počne uzimati vrijeme s obitelji, a to se ponekad ne može izbjeći, točno zna koliko dugo i do koje mjere to smije trajati. Ako se situacija ne sredi, nešto će rezati, ali ne vrijeme s obitelji, nego posao. Pa će onda, dodaje, vidjeti koliko će davati desetine „ili još više“ da se to nadoknadi. Sve se, zaključuje, svodi na pitanje kakav želi biti kao čovjek pred Bogom i pred svojom obitelji.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: ljudsko dostojanstvo ne proizlazi iz titule ili prihoda, a odgovorno supružništvo, očinstvo i briga za obitelj opravdano se stavljaju u središte životnog razlučivanja. Jedina nejasnoća jest može li se spominjanje desetine shvatiti kao da novčano davanje može nadoknaditi zanemarivanje obiteljskih obveza; to ne bi bilo u skladu s naglaskom Crkve na stvarnom, skladnom usklađivanju rada i obiteljskog života.
concerns: Izraz da će se davanjem desetine „nadoknaditi” gubitak vremena može, ako se misli doslovno, zamagliti činjenicu da se obiteljska odgovornost ne može jednostavno zamijeniti novcem ili milostinjom.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk potvrđuje da čovjekova vrijednost počiva u njegovu osobnom dostojanstvu, a ne u vrsti posla koji obavlja. Istodobno, rad nije samo nužno sredstvo zarade: može biti služenje obitelji i društvu te sudjelovanje u Božjem stvaralačkom djelu, pa je cilj ravnoteža rada, obitelji i odmora, a ne omalovažavanje rada.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mostly aligned with Catholic teaching: human dignity does not derive from title or income, and responsible spousal life, fatherhood, and family care are rightly placed at the center of life discernment. The only ambiguity is whether mentioning tithing can be understood as monetary giving compensating for the neglect of family obligations; that would not align with the Church's emphasis on a real, harmonious balance between work and family life.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching confirms that a person's worth rests in their personal dignity, not in the type of work they perform. At the same time, work is not merely a necessary means of earning: it can be a service to family and society and participation in God's creative work, so the goal is a balance of work, family, and rest, not denigration of work.
concerns_en: The phrase that by giving a tithe one will "make up" for lost time can, if meant literally, obscure the fact that family responsibility cannot simply be replaced with money or alms.

sections.subtitle_en: Who Am I Without a Title? Son of God, Husband, and Dad
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mislav says that at conferences he first introduces himself as a son of God, husband, and dad
sections.content_en:
Mislav says that he had to ask that question to himself and that it is a frequent motif in his videos. He looked for the answer on paper. On one side he put everything he could give up: the possibility of buying an estate, its renovation, finances, business. On the other side he wrote down what he truly wants. One thing repeated itself: **more time with family, healthy upbringing of the child, and a healthy relationship with the wife**.

He realized that everything he is giving up is tied to something monetary and earthly, which as a person gives him no worth whatsoever. "It's even worse," he admits, because he wasn't proving himself to others, but to himself.

Today, when he speaks at conferences and lectures, he does not state the title first. He says: **"I am above all a son of God, I want to be a husband, I want to be a dad."** The fact that he is a consultant is only the way in which he secures sustenance. He could have been anything, and he chose what he knows how to do. It would be "a bit pointless" to study to be a carpenter now, "although it would be cool."

He also set a clear boundary, as he says, a "cap." If work starts taking away time with his family again, and that sometimes cannot be avoided, he knows exactly how long and to what extent that is allowed to last. If the situation is not sorted out, he will cut something, but not time with family, rather work. And then, he adds, he will see how much tithe he will give "or even more" to make up for it. Everything, he concludes, comes down to the question of what kind of man he wants to be before God and before his family.

sections.subtitle: Franovo zadovoljstvo, hrast iza Mislava i poruka Plenkoviću
sections.screenshot_description: Fran se smije stablu postavljenom iza Mislava, poznatijeg kao Tata Hrast
sections.content:
Marko pita Frana što ako ne uspije promijeniti svoju situaciju i ostane na sadašnjem poslu. Fran se najprije našali da će kolege iz firme, ako gledaju podcast, svakako čuti da ostaje.

Ozbiljnije odgovara da zarađuje dovoljno za sebe i obitelj, a to mu je glavni životni cilj. Volio bi imati više vremena s obitelji i ne putovati sat vremena na posao, otkako su se odselili izvan grada. Ipak ne misli da bi time išta izgubio na vrijednosti, jer **zna tko je, bez obzira na posao koji radi**. Na Markovo dodatno pitanje je li zadovoljan odgovara da jest. Muči ga samo poslovni plan, a osobni život, ono što ima kod kuće i što radi u zajednici, dovoljno mu je.

Usred odgovora prekida sam sebe. Od početka snimanja ne može se koncentrirati jer je iza Mislava, poznatog kao Tata Hrast, postavljeno stablo. „I onda je ovo hrast, znači ja umirem“, smije se. Marko mu ironično zahvaljuje što je to ubacio baš u ovom dijelu.

Fran zatim upućuje i šaljivu poruku Andreju Plenkoviću i ekipi: neka uvedu šest sati radnog vremena i neradne petke. Kad mu Marko kaže da to predloži šefu, Fran odgovara da to mora doći „s vrha“, za cijelu državu. Mislav ga pita radi li u privatnom sektoru i znakovito spominje HEP, a Fran zaključuje: „Eto, ušli smo i u politiku.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim pogledom jer Fran odvaja vlastitu vrijednost od zaposlenja, cijeni obiteljski život i zajednicu te izražava želju za većim vremenom s obitelji. Šaljivi prijedlog kraćeg radnog tjedna političko je i praktično mišljenje, a ne tvrdnja o katoličkom nauku; sam po sebi ne predstavlja teološki problem.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk ne suprotstavlja obitelj radu: rad može osiguravati život obitelji i služiti drugima, ali radni uvjeti trebaju poštovati osobu i omogućiti joj obiteljski, društveni i duhovni život. Zato je želja za kraćim radnim vremenom pitanje razborite prosudbe i javne politike, dok je načelo da gospodarstvo i rad trebaju služiti ljudskom dostojanstvu, a ne obratno.
